findings.function: convertToShares, convertToAssets, previewDeposit / Mint / Withdraw / Redeem, deposit, mint, redeem, withdraw, maxWithdraw (Math.mulDiv inlined)
findings.lines: e.g. convertToShares: the 'if _13 * assets + (mulmod(...) < _13 * assets) != mulmod(...)' block (165 lines in all)
findings.decompiled: if lastPricePerShare <= -1 * _13 * assets + mulmod(assets, _13, -1) - (...): revert with Panic(uint256), 17 ^ 3 * (not lastPricePerShare) / _14 = -6 * (lastPricePerShare / (lastPricePerShare & -lastPricePerShare)) * (2 ^ 3 * ...) ... / _18 = 2 * _16 * (...) - _16 * _16 * (...)
findings.source: OZ Math.mulDiv(assets, 10 ** decimals, lastPricePerShare) (512-bit multiply, Newton inverse of the odd part of the denominator)
findings.issue: Every conversion expands the full-precision mulDiv into five 400+ character lines of Newton-iteration algebra, and the panic code is the arithmetic '17 ^ 3 * (not lastPricePerShare)' (Panic 18 when the denominator is 0, else 17).
findings.rule: Known pattern P9. Recognise the 512-bit product (mulmod(a, b, -1) with the borrow) and the inverse-by-Newton sequence on d / (d & -d) as one exact operation mulDiv(a, b, d) with its overflow condition; c ^ k * (not x) is (c ^ k) if x == 0 else c.

notes: Clean apart from mulDiv. The only source loop is manage's (requiresAuth via authority.canCall or owner, then per target canCall + functionCallWithValue), shown as a while with the results zero-init rotated before it (P3). Each conversion function also has the compiler's checked exponentiation loop for 10 ** decimals ('while u > 1', 11 copies, P7) under 'if decimals >= 78 and decimals >= 32' (the second test implied, P11). Getters, ERC20 and admin functions checked.
summary: Faithful; the single source loop is a clean while, but the inlined mulDiv in every ERC-4626 conversion is expanded into unreadable algebra (P9).
